## Analytic sector and rectangular bends {#sec-elements-bends}

The OPALX `SBEND` and `RBEND` are field-based bend models. The reference
particle and the bunch are integrated through a magnetic field that is
evaluated in the element frame; bends are not tracked with transfer matrices.
The field has dipole and quadrupole terms, an Enge fringe field when
`HGAP > 0`, and a correction for the vertical edge focusing.

### Coordinates

The placed pose of a bend is the entrance frame used by its field model.
For `SBEND`, the local $z$ axis follows the design-orbit tangent at the
entrance. For `RBEND`, it is normal to the entrance pole face and follows
the straight magnet body; it generally differs from the incoming orbit
tangent. `ELEMEDGE` derives this element frame from the reference geometry,
while `X`…`PSI` specify its explicit pose.

- `SBEND`: positions are converted to bend coordinates $(x, y, s)$, where $s$
  is the arc length along the design orbit, from 0 at the entrance to $L$ at
  the exit, and $x$ is the radial offset from the design orbit. The field is
  evaluated in these coordinates and turned back into the entrance frame.
  The pole faces are perpendicular to the design orbit.
- `RBEND`: the field is evaluated in the straight frame of the magnet body,
  with $z$ from 0 at the entrance face to $L$ at the exit face. The design
  orbit crosses the faces at the pole-face angles `E1` and `E2`. If neither
  is specified, both are `ANGLE/2`. If one is specified, the other is
  derived so that `E1 + E2 = ANGLE`; specifying both requires that sum.
  Explicit pole-face angles require $L>0$, $|\mathrm{ANGLE}|<\pi$, and
  $|E_1|,|E_2|<\pi/2$.

### Field strength

The dipole strength is
$$
B_0 = \frac{P_0}{c\,q}\,K_0 ,
$$
where $P_0$ is the global `P0` (GeV/$c$, default 1) and $q$ the reference
charge in units of $e$. With these input units, the signed magnetic rigidity is
$$
(B\rho)_0[\mathrm{T\,m}]
=\frac{P_0[\mathrm{GeV}/c]}{0.299792458\,q}.
$$
Thus $B_0=(B\rho)_0K_0$ and $g=(B\rho)_0K_1$. In expressions using $P_0/c$,
the implementation first converts the input momentum from GeV/$c$ to eV/$c$
and uses $c$ in m/s. Dividing by $q$ makes the bend direction independent of
the charge sign. If `K0` is not given, it is derived from `ANGLE` $\theta$:
$$
K_0^{\mathrm{SBEND}} = \frac{\theta}{L},
\qquad
K_0^{\mathrm{RBEND}} = \frac{2\sin(\theta/2)}{L}
\quad\text{or}\quad \frac{\theta}{L_{\mathrm{arc}}}\ \text{with}\ E_1, E_2,
$$
where $L_{\mathrm{arc}}$ is the length of the design orbit between the two
faces. A given `K0` replaces this value. The quadrupole gradient is
$g = P_0 K_1/(c\,q)$, and the skew terms follow from `K0S` and `K1S` in the
same way. `K2`, `K3`, `K2S` and `K3S` are parsed but not applied.

For `RBEND`, a positive `DESIGNENERGY` $T_d$ (MeV) scales the field by
$p(T_d)/P_0$, with $p(T_d) = \sqrt{T_d(T_d + 2mc^2)}/c$ for the beam's rest
mass. Form the ratio $p(T_d)/P_0$ with both momenta in the same units;
`DESIGNENERGY` is entered in MeV while `P0` is entered in GeV/$c$.
`SBEND` rejects `DESIGNENERGY`. `P0` should therefore be set to the
reference momentum of the beam.

### Longitudinal profile

With the full gap $g_{\mathrm{gap}} = 2\,$`HGAP` (or `GAP` for `RBEND`), the field
is multiplied by an Enge function of the distance $d$ past a pole face
($d < 0$ inside the magnet),
$$
F(d) = \frac{1}{1 + \exp\!\left(\sum_{i=0}^{5} c_i\,(d/g_{\mathrm{gap}})^i\right)},
$$
with the OPAL default coefficients
$c = (0.478959,\ 1.911289,\ -1.185953,\ 1.630554,\ -1.082657,\ 0.318111)$.
$F \to 1$ inside the magnet, $F \to 0$ outside, and $F \approx 0.38$ at the face.
Of the entrance and exit values, the smaller one is used. The field extends
$5\,g_{\mathrm{gap}}$ before the entrance face and past the exit face; beyond
that it is zero. With `HGAP = 0` the edge is hard: $F = 1$ on $[0, L)$ and the
field is zero elsewhere.

`RBEND` can instead read a `1DProfile1` profile through `FMAPFN`; its amplitude
is then set so that the design orbit bends by `ANGLE`. This is a separate
profile-dipole model: explicitly specifying `K0`, `K0S`, `K1`, `K1S`, `K2`,
`K2S`, `K3`, `K3S` or `FINT` with that profile is rejected, even when the
explicit value is zero. Its fringe field comes from the profile derivatives;
the native finite-gap correction below is not added. See the
[field-map appendix](../../user-guide/appendix/field-maps/index.qmd#opalx-rbend-profile).

### Field in and near the magnet

For the native analytic normal terms, let $F'$ and $F''$ be derivatives
with respect to the longitudinal field coordinate ($s$ for `SBEND`, $z$ for
`RBEND`):
$$
\begin{aligned}
B_y &= B_0\left(F - \tfrac12 F''\,y^2\right) + g\,F\,x,\\
B_s &= B_0\,F'\,y,\\
B_x &= g\,F\,y + C\,F'\,y .
\end{aligned}
$$
The $F''$ and $F'$ terms keep the dipole fringe field free of sources to
first order in $y$. They give the geometric edge focusing, including the
$h\tan E$ term of a rotated pole face.

The last term, with coefficient $C$, adds the finite-gap correction to the
vertical edge focusing. With signed curvature $h = \theta/L_{\mathrm{arc}}$ and
pole-face angle $E$,
$$
\psi = h\,\frac{g_{\mathrm{gap}}}{2}\,F_{\mathrm{int}}\,\frac{1 + \sin^2 E}{\cos E},
\qquad
\Delta k_y = h\left[\tan E - \tan(E - \psi)\right],
$$
For a nonzero curvature, define the profile span
$$
D=\left|F(-5g_{\mathrm{gap}})-F(5g_{\mathrm{gap}})\right|.
$$
The coefficient multiplying the longitudinal derivative $F'$ is
$$
C=\begin{cases}
+(B_0/h)\,\Delta k_{y,\mathrm{in}}/D,&\text{entrance-limited profile},\\
-(B_0/h)\,\Delta k_{y,\mathrm{out}}/D,&\text{exit-limited profile}.
\end{cases}
$$
The opposite signs compensate for the rising entrance and falling exit
profiles. $F_{\mathrm{int}}$ is `FINT`. For `SBEND`, $E=0$; for `RBEND`,
use `E1` at the entrance and `E2` at the exit. The native correction is
zero when `FINT = 0`, the full gap is zero, or the reference curvature is zero.

### Aperture

With `HGAP > 0` the bend gets a rectangular aperture of half-height `HGAP`;
`HAPERT` sets its horizontal half-width, which is otherwise unlimited. An
`APERTURE` string may replace `HAPERT` if its vertical half-width does not
exceed `HGAP`. Particles outside the aperture get no field, and are removed if
they are inside the body, $0 \le s < L$.

### `SBEND` and `RBEND` class structure

The current implementation splits bend handling into a parser-facing object layer
and a runtime representation layer. `OpalSBend` and `OpalRBend` inherit the
common bend attributes and update logic from `OpalBend`, then instantiate and
configure `SBendRep` and `RBendRep` respectively.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-elements-bend-class-diagram
%%| fig-cap: "Parser-side and runtime-side class structure for the current OPALX `SBEND` and `RBEND` implementation."
classDiagram
  direction TB

  class OpalElement

  class OpalBend {
    +print(os)
  }

  class OpalSBend {
    +OpalSBend()
    +clone(name)
    +update()
  }

  class OpalRBend {
    +OpalRBend()
    +clone(name)
    +update()
  }

  class ElementBase

  class SBend {
    +apply(pc)
    +setFieldComponents(normal, skew)
  }

  class RBend {
    +apply(pc)
    +setFieldComponents(normal, skew)
    +setFieldMap(filename)
  }

  class SBendRep {
    +clone()
    +getGeometry()
  }

  class RBendRep {
    +clone()
    +getGeometry()
  }

  class Geometry
  class BendFieldModel {
    <<namespace>>
    +bendField(arc, inputs)
    +engeProfile(d, gap)
  }

  OpalElement <|-- OpalBend
  OpalBend <|-- OpalSBend
  OpalBend <|-- OpalRBend

  ElementBase <|-- SBend
  ElementBase <|-- RBend
  SBend <|-- SBendRep
  RBend <|-- RBendRep

  OpalSBend ..> SBendRep : creates/configures
  OpalRBend ..> RBendRep : creates/configures

  SBendRep *-- Geometry : geometry_m
  RBendRep *-- Geometry : geometry_m
  SBend ..> BendFieldModel : uses
  RBend ..> BendFieldModel : uses
```

`OpalSBend` and `OpalRBend` read the input and set up `SBendRep` and
`RBendRep`. These hold the `Geometry` and the field coefficients; `SBend` and
`RBend` evaluate the field with the functions in `BendFieldModel`.
